name: Afudius
body:
Afudius
CR 1

This long, muscular snake rears revealing its devilish horns and fangs when threatened. It is mottled pitch black and fiery red in color, with bright eyes in a broad head.

XP 400
N Tiny animal
Init +5; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +11

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 17, flat-footed 14 (+5 Dex, +2 natural, +2 size)
hp 11 (2d8+2)
Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +3

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., climb 20 ft., swim 20 ft.
Melee bite +8 (1d2-1 plus poison and fanged phlebotomy)
Space 2 1/2 ft.; Reach 0 ft.

STATISTICS

Str 8, Dex 21, Con 12, Int 1, Wis 17, Cha 6
Base Atk +1; CMB -2; CMD 13
Feats Weapon Finesse
Skills Climb +13, Perception +11, Stealth +17, Swim +13; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Fanged Phlebotomy (Ex)

When an afudius hits with its bite, a living creature with blood takes 1 point of Constitution damage.

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 12; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d3 Con damage; cure 1 save.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm desert, mountains, or plains
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

Sometimes also called a haemorrhois, an afudius is small, just over a foot long, with males having multiple bristling horns and females a single off-center horn. Its scales are rough and make a rustling sound as the snake moves. They are slow and sluggish animals and make winding nests in rocky areas.

Envenomation by an afudius is particularly gruesome. As the venom spreads, blood begins to leave by every opening possible, draining out through the eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth, even the very pores. Scars reopen. Teeth and nails fall out.

The entire body becomes one bleeding wound, and death comes through catastrophic blood loss.
